B. Bath. 92ᵇ כי אזלינן בתר רובא בא׳ בממונא לא we follow the majority principle (that a doubtful thing is presumed to have the legal status of the majority of its class) only in ritual questions, but not in civil law.—עבד א׳ to commit a crime, euphem. for prostitution, &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 60b:21">Sabb. 60ᵇ</cite> <he>בבלאי שרי א׳</he> a Babylonian permitter of forbidden things (R. Ḥiya).—

<cite ref="Niddah 24b:2">Nidd. 24ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>הלכתא כרב בא׳</he> Rab is the adopted authority in ritual law. [<cite ref="Kiddushin 12a:9">Kidd. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>זול איסורי</he> &c. read <he>אִיסָרֵי</he>; v. <cite ref="A01506"><he>אִיסָר</he></cite>.]
